transcript.text: my samsung washer dryer is making evrything smell damp/musty even after its washed, its gross. wot do i do

That damp/musty smell is usually mildew/biofilm somewhere in the washer, or clothes staying damp too long in the drying cycle. It’s very fixable.

### Do this first
1. Take out any laundry and leave the door open.
2. Clean the rubber door seal (gasket)
   Pull back the folds carefully and wipe out hair, lint, sludge, coins etc. Use hot soapy water or a washing-machine cleaner. Wipe underneath it too.
3. Clean the detergent drawer
   Remove it if your model allows, wash it in hot water and scrub the compartments. Also wipe inside the drawer housing.
4. Clean the drain/pump filter (usually behind a small flap at the bottom front)
   Put towels and a shallow tray down first — water will come out. Remove lint, buttons, gunk etc., then refit it properly. Check your Samsung manual/model instructions if you’re unsure.

### Run a cleaning cycle
• Run Drum Clean / Eco Drum Clean / Drum Clean+ if your Samsung has it, empty.
• If it doesn’t, run the hottest, longest empty cycle available using a proper washing-machine cleaner.
• Don’t put clothes in during this.
• Don’t mix bleach, vinegar, descaler or other cleaners together — that can create dangerous fumes and damage the machine. Use one product exactly as directed.

Afterwards, run a normal hot wash with towels/rags if the cleaner instructions recommend rinsing.

### Prevent it coming back
• Use less detergent than you think, especially with concentrated liquid detergent. Too much leaves residue that feeds the smell.
• Avoid using fabric softener for a while; it can build up in washer-dryers.
• Do a 60°C wash occasionally (if the fabric allows). Constant 20–40°C washes encourage buildup.
• Take clothes out as soon as the cycle ends.
• Leave the door and detergent drawer slightly open between washes so the drum can dry.
• Wipe the door seal dry after washer-dryer use.
• Clean the filter and run Drum Clean roughly monthly, or when the machine prompts you.

### Because it’s a washer-dryer
If the clothes smell OK after washing but smell musty after drying, check:
• You aren’t overloading it — drying capacity is usually much lower than wash capacity.
• Clothes aren’t being left warm and damp in the machine after the dry ends.
• The drain filter is clean; poor draining can make drying smell stale.
• The room has some ventilation; washer-dryers generate lots of moisture.

### If it still smells after cleaning
If the smell returns immediately, there may be buildup in the internal drain hose/pump or a drainage issue. Also check whether water is sitting in the drum or the machine is draining slowly. At that point, a Samsung/washer repair engineer may need to clean or inspect the internal hoses and pump.

For now, I’d avoid washing anything important until you’ve cleaned the seal, drawer and pump filter, then run a Drum Clean.
